Keywords: Carpathian seasonal herding dairy and pasture rights
RagShortTexts: Mountain herding adjusts pastures with the seasons.
Passes, land rights and household labor constrain movement.

Variants.Content: Carpathian herding links seasonal pasture, dairy and passes. Animals and people need water, food and stops. High grass is not unrestricted access: permissions, young animals and carrying dairy products are part of movement.
Troops avoid scattering herds and check guides’ care duties. Borrowed pack animals need timely return or a household may miss its next pasture.
Dairy and pack demands follow seasons and herd capacity. Taking breeding animals reduces future returns; negotiated pasture and passage sustain ties better than treating all herders as guards.
Milking, processing, young stock and packing compete for labor. Exchanges with neighbors and recognized pasture access let households complete seasonal movement safely.
